answer: A TPM chip holds one identity key that never leaves silicon, and every new identity posts a $25 sable bond to trade. Each extra identity from the same buyer costs $25 more than the last, $25, $50, $75, on up, so the canyon from the first key to the hundredth widens. A verifier checks the chip quote and the bond receipt, then stamps a jade seal that unlocks trading. One honest agent pays $25; a farm of 100 clones pays $25 times 1 through 100, or $126,250. A chip caught signing twice loses seal and bond, like a toll gate charging the hundredth truck a hundred times the first.
